gloss: pass on, pass beyond; (particle) as far as, until; perpetuity; prey; (ornament)
summary: The root of passing on. The verb is to pass over or along (Job 28:8), in Aramaic to pass from or pass away, and causatively to take away (Dan 4:28; 7:14, 26). Its commonest word, עַד, says how far a thing goes on: "as far as, up to" of place, "until" of time (Lev 23:14, 16), "even to" of amount, and before a clause "until" or "while"; as a noun עַד is the going on itself, perpetuity, "for ever" (Psa 37:29), and a second noun עַד is prey, what is fallen on and carried off (Gen 49:27). That the particle grows from this root is well supported, though no text shows the step: its poetic form עֲדֵי is built as עֲלֵי beside עַל of עלה; Ugaritic, Phoenician, Moabite, Sabaic and Akkadian all have ʿd or adi "until, as far as"; and Arabic ʿadā "pass from, pass beyond" and Sabaic ʿdw "enter, invade" are verbs of the same consonants, the Arabic one serving as a particle too. The ornaments עֲדִי and the verb "adorn" share the spelling, but how they join "passing on" is not clear.

words.gloss: as far as, up to; until; even to; (before a clause) until, while
words.summary: Taken as the bound form of a noun of עָדָה, "a going on (to)", fixed as a preposition: the poetic עֲדֵי (Psa 104:23; Job 7:4; Psa 147:6) is the same form as עֲלֵי, אֱלֵי beside עַל, אֶל. It names the far point of a reach, a span of time or an amount, and before a clause the point up to which something lasts. Its counterpart in scripture's Aramaic and in the Peshitta is the same word (below).

senses.gloss: as far as, up to, to (a place or person)
senses.definition: The point a border, a journey or a reach goes on to.

evidence.note: The Canaanite border "from Sidon … as far as Gaza … as far as Lasha".
The spies explore "from the wilderness of Zin as far as Rehob".
"that my salvation may be to (עַד) the end of the earth"; quoted in Act 13:47.
עַד לַשָּׁמָיִם: "our guilt has grown up to the heavens".
"the matter of both shall come to (עַד) God": to a person.
The poetic form: Yahweh brings the wicked "down to (עֲדֵי) the ground".

senses.definition: The time something lasts up to: the end of a span, with the time named.

evidence.note: No new bread or grain "until (עַד) this very day, until (עַד) you have brought the offering of your God": the firstfruits sheaf marks the end of the restriction.
"Up to (עַד) the morrow after the seventh sabbath you shall count fifty days": the count runs up to the day of the new grain offering.
The Day of Covering is kept "from evening until (עַד) evening".
The waters went on decreasing "until the tenth month".
Man goes out to his labour "until (עֲדֵי) evening".
Yahweh has not given them a heart to know "to (עַד) this day"; quoted in Rom 11:8.
The words are sealed "until the time of the end".

senses.definition: With מָתַי "when?" or אָנָה "whither?": up to when will a thing go on? A complaint or a rebuke.

evidence.note: "How long (עַד־אָנָה) will this people spurn me?"
"How long (עַד־מָתַי), Lord?" and the answer "until (עַד אֲשֶׁר אִם) cities lie waste".
"How long, Yahweh, will you forget me?", twice.

senses.definition: With עוֹלָם or the noun עַד: up to a time with no end in view, for ever.

evidence.note: Samuel is to be seen before Yahweh "and dwell there for ever (עַד־עוֹלָם)", for life.
"Trust in Yahweh for ever (עֲדֵי־עַד), for in Yah, Yahweh, is a rock of ages".
"Rejoice for ever (עֲדֵי־עַד) in what I create".
Zion: "this is my rest for ever (עֲדֵי־עַד); here I will dwell".

senses.gloss: even to, as many as, to the point of
senses.definition: How far an amount or a degree goes: "as many as", "exceedingly"; with a negative, עַד־אֶחָד is "not even one".

evidence.note: Isaac trembled "a great trembling, to (עַד) excess" (עַד־מְאֹד).
"Not even one (עַד־אֶחָד) of Israel's livestock died".
"Not even one was left".
The boy sneezed "as many as (עַד) seven times".
Uzziah grew strong "exceedingly" (עַד־לְמָעְלָה).

senses.gloss: from … to: all, both … and (מִן … וְעַד)
senses.definition: After a first term with מִן it names the far end of a range, and the pair takes in all between: everyone, of every kind.

evidence.note: "from man and to woman, from young and to old": everyone in Jericho.
"They will all know me, from the least of them to (וְעַד) the greatest"; quoted in Heb 8:11.
"All Israel from Dan to (וְעַד) Beersheba".
Nothing missing "from small to great".

senses.definition: Before a clause, bare or joined by אֲשֶׁר, כִּי or אִם, or before an infinitive: up to the time when something happens.

evidence.note: "The sceptre will not turn aside from Judah … until (עַד כִּי) Shiloh comes".
"Sit at my right hand until (עַד) I make your enemies a footstool for your feet"; quoted in Mat 22:44 and Heb 1:13.
"I will not leave you until (עַד אֲשֶׁר אִם) I have done what I have spoken".
"until (עַד כִּי) he became very great".
"Sit, my daughter, until you know how the matter falls".
The Kohathites set out carrying the holy things, and the others set up the dwelling "against their coming" (עַד־בֹּאָם): by the time they arrived.
"until (עַד) he comes whose is the judgment, and I will give it".
עַד־בִּלְתִּי: "until the heavens are no more".
עַד־בְּלִי: "abundance of peace until the moon is no more".

senses.definition: Of a span still running: while, whilst.

evidence.note: "Was not this my word while (עַד) I was still in my own land?"
"While (עַד) Saul was speaking to the priest, the tumult … grew".
"While (עַד) this one was speaking, another came".
"While the king was at his table".
ἕως for עַד: "until this very day".
ἕως for עַד־אָשִׁית.
Psa 110:1 quoted: ἕως ἂν θῶ τοὺς ἐχθρούς σου.
Psa 110:1 again.
Jer 31:34: ἀπὸ μικροῦ αὐτῶν ἕως μεγάλου αὐτῶν.
Deu 29:3: ἕως τῆς σήμερον ἡμέρας.
Isa 49:6: ἕως ἐσχάτου τῆς γῆς.
עַד־עֶצֶם הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה, "until this very day".
"until now (עַד־כֹּה) you have not listened".
Ebenezer: "hitherto (עַד־הֵנָּה) Yahweh has helped us".

phrases.phrase: עַד אֲשֶׁר / עַד כִּי / עַד אִם

phrases.gloss: up to, as far as (doubled preposition)

evidence.note: "his word runs speedily".

words.summary: The going on itself: time that continues. It stands after a preposition (לָעַד "to perpetuity", עֲדֵי־עַד), as the second word of the pair לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד "for ever and ever", or bound after a noun, "perpetual mountains". Whether it has no end at all is said by what it is said of: Yahweh's reign and the king's throne (Exo 15:18; Psa 45:7), or a curse that lasts (Psa 9:6). Its link to the root is that of the particle: the time things go on to. The Ugaritic and Phoenician cognates show only the phrase "until ʿlm", for ever, not the noun alone.

senses.definition: Time going on with no end set; with לְ or עֲדֵי, "for ever".

evidence.note: "The righteous will inherit the land and dwell upon it for ever (לָעַד)".
Yahweh's precepts "upheld for ever (לָעַד), for ever (לְעוֹלָם)": the two set side by side.
"His righteousness stands for ever (לָעַד)"; quoted in 2Co 9:9.
Words "cut in the rock for ever".
The king who judges the poor in truth: "his throne will be established for ever".
"He does not keep his anger for ever".
Written down "for a later day, for ever (לָעַד), to perpetuity (עַד־עוֹלָם)".

senses.definition: Joined after עוֹלָם, the two together say it as strongly as the language can.

evidence.note: "Yahweh will reign for ever and ever".
"Your throne, O God, is for ever and ever"; quoted in Heb 1:8.
The wicked nations' name blotted out "for ever and ever".
Those who turn many to righteousness shine "like the stars for ever and ever".

senses.definition: Bound after a noun, of what lasts: the abiding mountains; Yahweh "who inhabits perpetuity"; the child named "father of perpetuity".

evidence.note: הַרְרֵי־עַד "the perpetual mountains" beside גִּבְעוֹת עוֹלָם "the everlasting hills".
שֹׁכֵן עַד: "who inhabits perpetuity".
אֲבִי־עַד: "father of perpetuity", one of the names of the child born to sit on David's throne (v. 6).
αἰῶνος for וָעֶד.
Psa 45:7: ὁ θρόνος σου, ὁ θεός, εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα τοῦ αἰῶνος.
Psa 112:9: ἡ δικαιοσύνη αὐτοῦ μένει εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα.

parallels.note: everlasting time: set side by side with עַד, and joined with it in לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד.

evidence.note: The wicked destroyed for ever.

words.summary: Three uses only. Benjamin the wolf devours עַד in the morning and divides שָׁלָל, spoil, at evening (Gen 49:27), and in Isa 33:23 עַד־שָׁלָל is "prey of spoil". In Zep 3:8 the pointing reads לְעַד "for the prey", but the same letters read לְעֵד are "as a witness", so that verse is uncertain. Its link to the root is the falling upon and carrying off that the same consonants mean in Arabic (ʿadā ʿalā, of a thief and of a wolf), Sabaic (ʿdw "invade, raid") and the Peshitta's Syriac (ʿdā "seize, come upon"); this is argued from the cognates, not shown in Hebrew.

senses.definition: What a beast of prey or a victor seizes and carries off.

evidence.note: "Benjamin is a wolf that tears; in the morning he devours prey (עַד), and at evening he divides spoil (שָׁלָל)".
"Then prey of abundant spoil (עַד־שָׁלָל) is divided; the lame take the plunder".
"Wait for me … for the day I rise up to the prey (לְעַד)"; the letters can also be read לְעֵד, "as a witness".

words.gloss: pass over, pass along; (hiphil) take off, take away
words.summary: Twice only in Hebrew. The lion has not passed over the path to wisdom, beside "trodden" (Job 28:8); the hiphil is to take a garment off on a cold day (Pro 25:20), making it pass from someone. Scripture's Aramaic verb of the same root (below) is used more, "pass from, pass away" and "take away", and gives the sense its fuller witness.

senses.definition: Of a beast going over or along a path.

evidence.note: "The proud beasts have not trodden it (הִדְרִיכֻהוּ); the lion has not passed over it (עָדָה עָלָיו)".

senses.definition: Make something pass away from someone: take a garment off.

evidence.note: מַעֲדֶה בֶּגֶד בְּיוֹם קָרָה: "one who takes off a garment on a cold day", like singing songs to a heavy heart.
παρῆλθεν for עָדָה.

parallels.note: tread: the beasts have not trodden it, the lion not passed over it.

words.summary: Always of decking with ornaments: most often a woman, or Israel or Jerusalem pictured as one (Ezk 16:11, 13; Hos 2:15; Jer 31:4), once Job, challenged to deck himself with majesty (Job 40:10). It is spelled as עָדָה "pass on", but how adorning joins passing on is not clear. One reading is "put on", the counterpart of the hiphil "take off" (Pro 25:20), and Hos 2:15 "she put on her ring" fits it, but no verse or cognate shows it; Aramaic עֲדִי "what is put on, cloak, ornament" is the nearest, and it may come from the Hebrew.

senses.definition: Put ornaments on oneself or on another; with the ornament as object, put it on.

evidence.note: "I decked you with ornaments (וָאֶעְדֵּךְ עֶדִי), and put bracelets on your hands and a chain on your neck".
"though you clothe yourself in scarlet, though you deck yourself with ornaments of gold".
וַתַּעַד נִזְמָהּ וְחֶלְיָתָהּ: "she put on her ring and her jewellery" and went after her lovers.
"You were decked with gold and silver".
"you painted your eyes and decked yourself with ornaments".
"as a bride adorns herself with her jewels".
"again you will deck yourself with your tambourines".
"Deck yourself with majesty and dignity", beside "clothe yourself (תִּלְבָּשׁ) with splendour".
κατεκόσμησεν for תַּעְדֶּה.
ἐκόσμησα for וָאֶעְדֵּךְ.
The new Jerusalem "prepared as a bride adorned (κεκοσμημένην) for her husband", the picture of Isa 61:10.
The holy women "adorned themselves", not with gold but with a quiet spirit.

parallels.note: clothe: adorning and clothing set side by side.

words.summary: Ornaments worn on the body or the clothing, gold above all (2Sa 1:24; Jer 4:30), a bride's especially (Jer 2:32; Isa 49:18). Israel took theirs off at Horeb, mourning at Yahweh's word that he would not go up among them (Exo 33:4–6). Three uses are difficult (Psa 32:9; 103:5; Ezk 16:7). Its link to the root is not clear (see the verb "adorn"). The BDB key's count also takes in בַּעֲדִי "behind, about, for me" (Exo 8:24; 1Ki 13:6; Psa 3:4; Lam 3:7 and others), which is בְּעַד, another word.

senses.definition: Ornaments put on and taken off: rings, bracelets, chains, gold on clothing.

evidence.note: "No man put his ornaments on him".
"Now take your ornaments off you, and I will know what to do with you".
"The sons of Israel stripped themselves of their ornaments from Mount Horeb onward".
Saul "put ornaments of gold on your clothing".
"Can a virgin forget her ornaments, a bride her sashes? Yet my people have forgotten me".
Zion's returning children: "you will put them all on like an ornament and bind them on like a bride".
"the beauty of his ornament he set in pride": the silver and gold of v. 19, made into images.
עֲדִי־זָהָב, "ornaments of gold".

senses.definition: Three verses where the sense "ornament" is hard to fit and the meaning is not settled.

evidence.note: Of a horse or mule, "whose עֲדִי is to be curbed with bit and bridle": perhaps its trappings, or its mouth.
"who satisfies your עֲדִי with good": the sense is not clear.
בַּעֲדִי עֲדָיִים: "you came to full ornament", perhaps "full beauty".
κόσμον for עֶדְיָהּ.
"Let your adorning (κόσμος) not be outward, braiding hair and putting on gold".

opposites.note: take down: "take your ornaments off you".

words.summary: עַד with הֵנָּה "hither": "up to here, up to now". Twice, both in Ecclesiastes, the second time shortened to עֲדֶן. Its tie to the root is the particle's own.

senses.definition: Up to the present: those still alive, and the one not yet born.

evidence.note: "the living who are still (עֲדֶנָה) alive".
"the one who has not yet (עֲדֶן) been".

words.gloss: until; as far as, to; as much as; (עַד דִּי) until
words.summary: The same particle in scripture's Aramaic, with the same senses; before a clause it takes דִּי, "until that".

senses.gloss: until (a time; with דִּי, a clause)
senses.definition: Up to a time, or up to the time when something happens.

evidence.note: "to speak lying words before me until (עַד דִּי) the time changes".
The horn prevailed "until the Ancient of Days came, and judgment was given to the saints".
"You watched until a stone was cut out, not by hands".
"I watched until thrones were set".
The work stopped "until the second year of Darius".
"from then until now (וְעַד־כְּעַן) it is being built".

senses.gloss: to, as far as; to the end
senses.definition: The point reached: a person approached, or the end of a thing.

evidence.note: One like a son of man "came to (עַד) the Ancient of Days, and they brought him near before him".
God's dominion is "to the end (עַד־סוֹפָא)".
The horn's dominion destroyed "to the end".
עַד־כָּה "here is the end of the matter".

senses.definition: With עָלַם: for ever.

evidence.note: God's name blessed "from age to age (מִן־עָלְמָא וְעַד עָלְמָא)".
The saints possess the kingdom "for ever, for ever and ever".

senses.definition: The most of an amount.

evidence.note: "up to a hundred talents of silver, up to a hundred cors of wheat …".

senses.definition: With דִּבְרַה "matter, cause": so that, in order that.

evidence.note: "to the end that the living may know that the Most High rules in the kingdom of men".

words.gloss: pass (from, onto); pass away; (haphel) take away, remove
words.summary: Scripture's Aramaic verb of the root, in Daniel: a smell passing onto clothes, a kingdom passing from a king, a law or a dominion that does not pass away; and causatively, God taking away kings and the beasts' dominion.

senses.definition: Go over from one place or holder to another.

evidence.note: "the smell of fire had not passed onto them (לָא עֲדָת בְּהוֹן)".
"The kingdom has passed from you (מַלְכוּתָה עֲדָת מִנָּךְ)".

senses.definition: Cease to stand: of a law revoked, or a dominion ended.

evidence.note: "the law of the Medes and Persians, which does not pass away", beside "not to be changed (לָא לְהַשְׁנָיָה)".
The son of man's "dominion is an everlasting dominion which will not pass away (לָא יֶעְדֵּה), and his kingdom one that will not be destroyed".

senses.definition: Make pass away: depose a king, take away glory or dominion.

evidence.note: God "removes kings and sets up kings" (מְהַעְדֵּה מַלְכִין וּמְהָקֵים מַלְכִין).
Nebuchadnezzar was brought down from his throne "and they took his glory from him".
The other beasts' dominion was taken away, yet their lives prolonged.
"They will take away his dominion, to destroy it to the end".

parallels.note: be destroyed (hithpaal): the kingdom that does not pass away is not destroyed.
be changed: the law that does not pass away is not to be changed.

opposites.note: set up: God removes kings and sets up kings.

words.summary: The Peshitta's ܥܰܕ (ʿad), mostly before a clause: "while".

senses.definition: Of a span still running.

evidence.note: "Agree with your adversary quickly, while (ܥܕ) you are with him on the way".
"I must work the works of him who sent me while it is day".
"Walk while you have the light".
John filled with the Holy Spirit "while he is in his mother's womb".

words.summary: The Peshitta's ܥܰܕܠܳܐ (ʿadlā), ʿad with lā "not": "while not yet", before.

senses.definition: While something has not yet happened.

evidence.note: "before they came together, she was found with child".
"your Father knows what you need before you ask him".
"before Philip called you … I saw you".

words.summary: The Peshitta's ܥܕܰܡܳܐ (ʿdammā), ʿad with mā: its usual "until", by which it renders Psa 110:1 where the Greek has ἕως.

senses.definition: Up to a time, a person or a point.

evidence.note: "he did not know her until she had brought forth her firstborn son".
Psa 110:1: "sit at my right hand until I put your enemies under your feet".
"from Abraham to David".

words.gloss: come upon, befall, seize; (aphel) take away
words.summary: The Peshitta's ܥܕܳܐ (ʿdā): a spirit seizing a boy, trials coming upon believers; in the aphel, taking a man away by force. It keeps the falling upon that Arabic ʿadā ʿalā and Sabaic ʿdw have, and the taking away of the Aramaic haphel.

senses.definition: Fall upon someone: of a spirit seizing, of trials befalling.

evidence.note: "a spirit seizes (ܥܕܝܐ) him, and suddenly he cries out".
"the trials which befell me through the plots of the Jews".
"the various trials that come upon you".

senses.definition: Carry someone off.

evidence.note: Lysias "with great violence took him away (ܐܥܕܝܗ) out of our hands".

cognates.gloss: pass from, pass beyond; exceed, transgress; (عَدَا, مَا عَدَا) except
cognates.note: A verb whose first sense is passing from one thing to another, or beyond a limit, and which also serves as a particle of exception ("they came, except Zeyd": what passes beyond the rest). The same consonants make a verb and a particle in Arabic as עָדָה and עַד are taken to do in Hebrew.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 1977, art. عدو, عَدَاهُ (n28369)
evidence.note: "He passed from it … to another … العَدْوُ primarily signifies Transition; … the going, or passing, beyond, or the exceeding, a limit"; "-A4- عَدَا is also a verb by which one makes an exception … جَآءَنِى القَوْمُ مَا عَدَا زَيْدًا".

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 1979, art. عدو, عَدَا (n28375)
evidence.note: "as a verb, or a preposition, or both, denoting an exception".

cognates.gloss: fall upon, act aggressively against; steal; (of a wolf, a beast of prey) that attacks men
cognates.note: The same verb with عَلَى "against": overstepping against someone, assailing, robbing. عَدَوَانٌ is said of a wolf that attacks men and عَادٍ of a beast of prey: the sense of עַד "prey" that Benjamin the wolf devours (Gen 49:27).

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 1977, art. عدو, عَدَاهُ (n28369), -b3- to -b6-
evidence.note: "He acted wrongfully … aggressively against him"; "said of a thief, He stole the goods"; "He leaped upon him, or it".

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 1980, art. عدو, عَدَوَانٌ (n28390)
evidence.note: "applied to a wolf … That acts aggressively against men"; سَبُعٌ عَادٍ, a beast of prey so called.

cognates.gloss: enter; invade, raid; break a law, trespass a boundary
cognates.note: Sabaic. Passing into a place, and passing over a limit: the city entered, the land raided, the boundary trespassed.

evidence.note: "(1) ENTER, often ENTER IN WAR > INVADE, MAKE A RAID … (2) BREAK a law, TRESPASS boundaries".

cognates.gloss: as far as, up to; in, at; (conj.) until
cognates.note: Sabaic, entered beside the verb ʿdw: "as far as the vicinity of the city"; "until he drove them into the sea".

evidence.note: "(1) AS FAR AS, UP TO"; conj. "UNTIL".

cognates.gloss: until, up to; (before a clause) until; (ʿd ʿlm) for ever
cognates.note: Segert counts it with ʿl "upon" among the prepositions ending in -ē, the form of Hebrew poetic עֲדֵי, עֲלֵי, and sets it beside Hebrew and Aramaic ʿad and Akkadian adi. He lists it apart from the adverb ʿd "still, yet" (cf. עוֹד).

evidence.note: "The preposition ʿd … 'until, to' … ʿd ʿlm (KTU 3.5:14) 'until/to eternity, for ever'".
As a conjunction: ʿd tšbʿ bk "until she is sated with weeping" (KTU 1.6 I 9).
"(H., Aram. ʿad, … Akkad. adi)".

cognates.gloss: as far as, up to; (conj.) until; (ʿd ʿlm) always, for ever
cognates.note: Phoenician and Punic: "I sailed upstream as far as SHRW"; "he ministered to the gods until becoming too weak"; ʿd ʿlm "for ever", as Hebrew עַד־עוֹלָם.

evidence.locator: p. 360, ʿD III prep. (CIS i 113.1) and conj. (CIS i 6000.5)
evidence.note: "AS FAR AS, UP TO"; conj. "UNTIL"; see also LMN … WʿD "from … to".
"ALWAYS, FOREVER".

cognates.gloss: until, as far as, up to; as long as, while; (with numbers) times
cognates.note: The commonest Akkadian word for "until", with the same reach as עַד: place, time, amount, and before a clause "until, while". Akkadian lost ʿ, so it cannot show the sound behind ע.

evidence.note: Senses include "as far as", "until", "up to", "as long as", "while", "times"; ×19016.

cognates.note: Jewish Aramaic of the Targums and Talmud: "up to six years of age" (B. Bath. 21a); עַד דְּ "until".

cognates.gloss: pass by, pass between; pass away, cease; (pael) remove; (ithpaal) be removed

cognates.note: Rabbinic (Talmud and Midrash), not the Targums; it may come from the Hebrew עֲדִי. If its sense "what is put on" is old, it would join the ornament words to the root as things put on, but nothing older shows it.

doctrine.statement: Yahweh tells David's lord, "Sit at my right hand until (עַד) I make your enemies a footstool for your feet" (Psa 110:1): the seat at the right hand is held up to a set point. The New Testament reads the Psalm of Jesus, raised and exalted (Act 2:34–35; Heb 1:13), who since then waits "until (ἕως) his enemies are made a footstool for his feet" (Heb 10:12–13), and whom heaven must receive "until (ἄχρι) the times of restoration of all things" (Act 3:21). The "until" of the Psalm therefore looks to his coming from heaven. After it he reigns "until he has put all enemies under his feet", death the last of them, and then hands the kingdom to the Father, that God may be all in all (1Co 15:24–28).

Jacob says the sceptre will not turn aside from Judah "until (עַד) Shiloh comes, and to him is the obedience of the peoples" (Gen 49:10). When the wicked prince of Israel is told to take off the turban and the crown, Yahweh says, "A ruin, a ruin, a ruin I will make it; this too shall not be, until (עַד) he comes whose is the judgment, and I will give it" (Ezk 21:30–32): David's throne in Jerusalem is left overturned up to the coming of the one it belongs to. The angel tells Mary that God will give Jesus "the throne of his father David", to reign over the house of Jacob for the ages, with no end to his kingdom (Luk 1:32–33). Daniel sees one like a son of man come to (עַד) the Ancient of Days and be given a dominion that "will not pass away (לָא יֶעְדֵּה)" (Dan 7:13–14), and the saints possess the kingdom "for ever, for ever and ever" (Dan 7:18, 22). The kingdom so promised is David's throne given to Christ and shared with his saints, and once given it does not pass away.

"The righteous will inherit the land and dwell upon it for ever (לָעַד)" (Psa 37:29). The same Psalm says the meek will inherit the land (Psa 37:11), and Jesus repeats it: "the meek will inherit the earth" (Mat 5:5). What is promised is a dwelling on the land that lasts, not a removal from the earth: the reward of the righteous is to live for ever on the earth they inherit.

Job says a man lies down and does not rise: "until (עַד) the heavens are no more" the dead will not wake or be roused from their sleep (Job 14:12). He asks God to hide him in the grave "until (עַד) your anger turns", to set him a time and remember him, and says he will wait all the days of his service "until (עַד) my change comes" (Job 14:13–14). In these verses death is a sleep in the grave lasting up to a set time; the dead man's hope is that God will remember him and his change will come, and nothing is said of a life carried on elsewhere in the meantime.

note: Drafted 2026-11-13 for Leviticus 23 (Lev 23:14 twice, 16, 32) and Numbers 10 (Num 10:21), where עַד is the particle. Root decision: the particle is keyed under עדה, the root of the verb עָדָה "pass on" and Aramaic עֲדָה "pass, pass away". Evidence for it: the poetic form עֲדֵי, a bound form of a III-weak noun like עֲלֵי (עַל, עלה) and אֱלֵי; Segert's Ugaritic class of prepositions in -ē (ʿd, ʿl); Arabic عدو ʿadā "pass from, pass beyond", which also serves as a particle of exception (Lane pp. 1977–1979); Sabaic ʿdw "enter, invade, trespass" beside the preposition ʿdy "as far as, until" (Biella pp. 352–354); the particle itself in Ugaritic, Phoenician, Moabite, Sabaic, Akkadian (adi) and all Aramaic. Against it, or not shown: no text shows the noun becoming the particle; Arabic has no ʿad "until" (its word is حَتَّى, not cognate) and Akkadian adi cannot show the ʿ. The alternative, that עַד goes with עוֹד "still, again" (root עוד, edut.json), is weaker: Segert lists Ugaritic ʿd "until" and ʿd "still, yet" apart, Arabic keeps ʿwd "return" and ʿdw "pass beyond" apart, and the -ē form points to a final weak radical, not a middle one. BDB keys: the keys here are filed by spelling, so the counts overlap and are too high: p.aq.ad (prep), p.aq.ab (perpetuity), p.aq.ac (prey) and xp.ac.aa (Aramaic עַד, root עד) each take in nearly all עַד tokens, Hebrew and Aramaic alike; p.aq.aa (pass on) and p.ar.aa (adorn) list the same 18 tokens, including the name Adah (Gen 4:19–23; 36:2–16) and Pro 25:20; p.ar.ac (ornament) includes בַּעֲדִי of בְּעַד (b.ce.ab: Exo 8:24; 1Ki 13:6; 2Ki 22:13; Psa 3:4; 138:8; Lam 3:7; 2Ch 34:21). Zero-token cross-references p.ao.ac, xp.aa.ag, p.ar.ak, p.ar.an, p.av.ad left out. Two verbs עָדָה are kept as two words of one entry (one spelling, one entry), since nothing yet joins "adorn" to "pass on". Left out: the names עָדָה Adah (p.ar.ab), עֲדָיָה Adaiah (p.ar.ae) and עֲדִיאֵל Adiel (p.ar.ad), BDB's "ornament" names, for name entries not written in this task; עֲדִיתַיִם Adithaim (p.ar.af), a place. Biblical Aramaic עִדָּן "time" (xp.ac.ab, root עדנ; Dan 7:25 "a time, times and half a time") is not taken in: the database keys it as its own root and yaad.json cites Akkadian adānu for it; whether it is a noun of עדה "passing (time)" is open. Peshitta: SEDRA lexemes 2243 ܥܕ (29 NT uses), 2244 ܥܕܠܐ (12), 2249 ܥܕܡܐ (219, root EDMA in SEDRA, taken here as ʿad with mā) and 2245 ܥܕܐ verb (4: Luk 9:39; Act 20:19; 24:7; 1Pe 1:6), found through nt_word; the vocalisations follow SEDRA. Sources read from text layers only: Segert pp. 78–80, 195; Krahmalkov pp. 359–361; Biella pp. 352–354 (check the scans). Not consulted: Dillmann or Leslau for Ge'ez ʿadawa "pass through, cross" (Biella's lead) and ʿadi; CAD A/1 adi; DULAT; Payne Smith or Brockelmann for Syriac ʿdā "seize, invade" and ʿad; CAL for Old and Imperial Aramaic ʿd. Open questions: (1) Zep 3:8 לְעַד "to the prey" or לְעֵד "as witness"; (2) Psa 32:9; 103:5; Ezk 16:7 עֲדִי; (3) whether the prey sense and the Syriac "seize" are kin (kin set on that reading); (4) the doctrine items are the reasoned reading and should be reviewed, especially Ezk 21:30–32 with Luk 1:32.
